author: travisgalloway
body:
Refs #201 (the standalone, non-training half — the parser-based over-repair prefix set; the fast/slow/both ablation half stays blocked on #200's trained model).

Resolves E4's "inconclusive by construction" over-repair result with a trustworthy real-code number.

## The result: over-repair on real code is real and non-trivial

| metric (slow-hard, 200 real-code prefixes, block 256, greedy) | value |
|---|---|
| raw `over_repair_rate` (any rollback on a clean_control row) | **0.260** — 2-3× the synthetic controls (Phase-0 0.083 / #199 0.101-0.120) |
| true over-repair (rollback \| the model's continuation was *actually* clean) | **13/36 = 0.36** |
| loop net clean-rate | 0.180 → 0.235 (still helps) |

On code the model already got right, the loop interrupts ~36% of the time — but it also fixes genuinely-broken continuations (baseline clean is only 18% at block-256), so it's a cost/benefit tradeoff, not pure damage. **The synthetic controls understated real-code over-repair.**

**Mechanism** (from transcripts): the spurious rollbacks are the frontier logic reinstating a *committed* `TS1xxx` syntax-incompleteness code (e.g. `TS1146`) as "real" at a segment boundary when `is_source_balanced` — but on multi-segment bodies that code is transient and resolves as generation continues. Tightening `is_source_balanced` is the concrete follow-up.

## How it got trustworthy — the three E4 confounds fixed
- **(b) mid-construct cuts** → `src/lsp/ts_boundaries.py`: tree-sitter-typescript returns only true top-level statement ends (new `[tree-sitter]` extra; imported lazily so the seam/import-guard are unaffected). `tests/test_ts_boundaries.py` proves no cut lands inside an unclosed construct.
- **(a) module resolution** → shared `MODULE_RESOLUTION_CODES` (`src/lsp/diagnostics.py`) + a portable `drop_codes` wrapper + `--ignore-module-resolution`, applied to **both** the in-loop diagnose and scoring (not just file selection).
- **(c) special-token leakage** → already handled by the harness EOS-stop under `budget=block`; **verified 0 leaks across all 600 transcript rows**.

## Also in this PR
- **Crash fix:** the slow loop did `filtered[0]` on an empty list when the only not-clean reason was a suppression hack (`as any` — ubiquitous in real TS); now marks unrepaired and stops. Regression test added. (Latent bug, exposed by `--ignore-module-resolution`.)
- New 200-prefix probe set `eval_sets/ts_error_injection/clean_prefixes.jsonl` (197 distinct repos, all brace/paren-balanced), replacing the 12 hand-authored controls.
- E4 design-doc section rewritten from "inconclusive" to the measured verdict.

## Testing
- [x] Full suite **821 passed / 6 skipped** (+10: tree-sitter boundary, `drop_codes`, crash regression)
- [x] Real run completed; `over_repair_rate` over 200 real-code rows; 0 special-token leaks
- [x] Probe set: 200 distinct prefixes, all balanced, cut at true top-level boundaries

author: asaomaro
body:
## 概要

対象拡張子が実務の実態と合っておらず、**実際に使われるソースの多くがどの機能の対象にもなっていなかった**。実機（pub400）のソースタイプ分布と実物の中身を根拠に修正した。

## 見つかった欠落

| 抜けていた拡張子 | 内容 | 実機での件数 |
|---|---|---|
| `.pf` / `.lf` | 物理ファイル / 論理ファイル（DDS） | 1038 / 666 |
| `.clle` | ILE CL | 219 |
| `.sqlrpgle` | SQL 組み込み ILE RPG | 209 |
| `.mnudds` | メニュー（DDS） | 72 |

**DDS は `.dds` というファイルを作らない**。実務ではオブジェクトの種類ごとに `.pf` / `.lf` / `.dspf` / `.prtf` を使う。`.dds` は保険として残した。

## 拡張子判定が4箇所に散っていた

`fileScope.ts` だけ直しても不十分だった。以下すべてに `.rpgle` / `.clp` 決め打ちがあり、**片方だけ足すとルーラーやプロンプターが効かない**。

- `fileScope.ts` の `TARGET_EXTENSIONS`（SOSI表示・ルーラー・診断の対象判定）
- `ruler.ts` の `specFamily`（桁ラベルの種別判定）
- `positionResolver.ts` の言語判定（F4プロンプター）
- `dialect.ts` の方言マップ（ILE / RPG III）

ruler と positionResolver は末尾一致の正規表現に変更し、追加漏れが起きにくい形にした。`dialect.ts` は長い拡張子から照合する既存の仕組みに乗せ、`.sqlrpg` が `.rpg` と誤判定されないようにしている。

## 追加可否は実物を見て判断した

**MNUDDS → 追加する**

```
     A* Free Form Menu: MENU1
     A                                      DSPSIZ(24 80 *DS3
     A                                      INDARA
```

6桁目が `A`、キーワードが44桁目からで、**DSPF と同じ A仕様書の固定長**だった。ルーラーも SOSI も他の DDS と同じ扱いで意味を持つ。

**BND → 追加しない**

```
/*-
 * Copyright (c) 2001-2020 Scott C. Klement
```

バインダー言語（`STRPGMEXP`/`EXPORT`/`ENDPGMEXP`）で、C風コメントで始まる**自由形式**。桁位置に意味が無くルーラーが機能しない。PJ の対象言語にも含まれない。27件の多くは `QSRVSRC` に置かれたサードパーティ製品の同梱物だった。

**その他の対象外**: `MNUCMD`（メニューのコマンド定義側。DDS ではない）、`RPG36`/`RPG38`/`CBL36`（System/36・38 互換の移行資産）、`CBLLE`/`CBL`/`C`/`CPP`/`PLI`（件数は多いが本PJの対象言語ではない）。

判断の根拠と理由は AGENTS.md に記録し、後から追えるようにした。

## 下流波及の点検

`AGENTS.md` の規約に沿って点検した。

- **診断**は `languageId === "cl"` または `.clp` のときだけ発火するため、新しい拡張子に CL 診断は走らない（意図しない診断の波及なし）。
- **言語登録**（`contributes.languages`）は変更していない。新しい拡張子に RPG/CL の言語機能（コメントトグル・タブナビ等）は付かない。「表示系のみ拡張し言語登録は広げない」という現行方針を維持している。

## 最終的な対象拡張子（13種）

```
rpg rpgle sqlrpgle sqlrpg     RPG（固定長）
clp clle                      CL
pf lf dspf prtf mnudds dds    DDS
cmd                           コマンド定義
```

## 動作確認

- [x] 型チェック / 構造検証288ファイル / CL往復（日英）/ RPG往復
- [x] 新しい拡張子が対象になり、`.bnd` `.rpg36` が対象外であること
- [x] `.sqlrpgle`→ile、`.sqlrpg`→rpg3 と方言が正しく解決されること

## 本PRに含まれないもの

**DDS の桁ラベルとプロンプターは依然として未実装。** `.pf` や `.mnudds` を開いても効くのは SOSI 表示とルーラーの目盛り段だけで、A仕様書の桁ラベルは出ない。実質的な DDS 対応はこれから。

author: clevengermatt
body:
Connect uses the same canonical code set as gRPC, so its error mapping now
mirrors the gRPC table the binding-invoker contract pins:
- unavailable, resource_exhausted -> ERR_UNAVAILABLE (transient; the server
  answered but refused as retryable, not a transport failure that never
  reached a server)
- canceled -> ERR_CANCELLED
Previously unavailable -> ERR_CONNECT_FAILED (semantically dishonest: the
server answered) and resource_exhausted/canceled fell to ERR_EXECUTION_FAILED
(service, not their true transient/cancelled categories). Genuine dial and
redirect failures still surface ERR_CONNECT_FAILED, unchanged.

body:
## 概要

前 PR（#10）で README に「価格は Yahoo 一択ではない／J-Quants を使おう」と書きましたが、実際には価格取得 CLI は `fetch_prices` が **yfinance 固定** で J-Quants を使えませんでした。本 PR で **README の推奨が実際に動くように**し、あわせて無料データ入手の実践ガイドと「無料リアルタイムの限界」ナレッジを追加します。

## 1. 価格ソースの切替（コア）

### `stocklib/data.py`
- `resolve_source()` … 優先順位 **`--source` 引数 > 環境変数 `STOCK_HACKER_SOURCE` > 既定 `yfinance`**。
- `set_default_source()` … CLI の `--source` を環境変数に反映し、`stocklib` 内部経由の `fetch_prices` にも一括適用。
- `add_source_argument()` … 各 CLI 共通の `--source` フラグ。
- `fetch_prices(..., source=...)` … `jquants` は `_fetch_one_jquants` にディスパッチ。**日足のみ**対応で、指数（`^N225`）・為替（`USDJPY=X`）は J-Quants 非対応のため **yfinance に自動フォールバック**。キャッシュはソース別に分離。
- `synthetic=True` は `source` より優先。`fetch_info`（PER/PBR 等）は yfinance 固定（切替は OHLCV のみ）。

### CLI 配線（11本）
`analyze_stock` / `compare` / `screen` / `run_backtest` / `daily_brief` / `portfolio_review` / `income_report` / `tax_report` / `performance_report` / `adr_parity` / `research_journal`（new・verify）に `--source {yfinance,jquants}` を追加。

### 使い方
```bash
python3 analysis/analyze_stock.py 7203 --source jquants   # コマンドごと
export STOCK_HACKER_SOURCE=jquants                        # セッション全体
```

## 2. ドキュメント / ナレッジ

- **`docs/data-sources.md`（新設）** … 無料でデータを見る/取る実践ガイド（ブラウザで見る → CLI で機械処理 → J-Quants 切替手順 → EDINET 一次情報 → 無料の限界）。目的別フローと具体コマンド付き。
- **`knowledge/data-sources/data-apis-and-tools.md`** … 「無料でリアルタイムに近い株価を得ることの限界」節を追加（鮮度の階層、無料リアルタイム API が存在しない構造的理由、鮮度×機械処理×無料のトリレンマ、バックテストと発注判断を混同しない線引き）。既存文書への追記のため索引変更なし。
- `README.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `.env.example` … 切替手順・制約（要トークン・日足のみ・**12週間遅延**・指数/為替フォールバック）と新 docs への導線を追記。

## テスト
`analysis/tests/test_data.py` にソース解決・不正値拒否・J-Quants ディスパッチ（モック）・指数フォールバック・日足以外ガード・キャッシュ分離・`synthetic` 優先を追加（環境変数汚染を防ぐ autouse フィクスチャ付き）。**全 531 テスト green**。

- `STOCK_HACKER_SOURCE=jquants` … env 経路でも反映。

author: mayswill3
body:
Turns an accepted challenge into an actually-played, settled match — the missing
last mile after Accept.

## What changed
- `listMyMatches` + `matches[]` on `GET /api/lobby/invites` (read-only): the
  caller's joinable MATCHED bets.
- Accepter routes to `/play/<gameType>?bet=<betId>` on Accept; the idle
  challenger is routed by the SAME ambient poll that delivered the challenge
  (a `routedBetIds` guard prevents double-navigation).
- Game pages resume from `?bet=` via `useResumeMatch` → `setup()` (return value
  used to avoid an authState race) then `joinFromLobby` (idempotent, so
  session-already-started / bet-already-resolved races are safe; a non-joinable
  bet falls back to the normal lobby UI). `/play` is `force-dynamic`.
- No-show void: the `bet-expiry` worker now voids MATCHED bets left unplayed
  past the orphan window and refunds both players.

## ⚠️ Reviewer: read `src/lib/lobby/match-lifecycle.ts` → `voidNoShowMatch` closely
This is a NEW point where **escrowed funds are released**. It lives under
`lobby/` rather than `ledger/`, so it may read like ordinary lobby code — it is
not. It sets a MATCHED bet to VOIDED and calls `refundEscrow` for BOTH players.
It reuses the existing `refundEscrow` primitive and mirrors the established
void pattern already in `/api/demo/cleanup-bets` and `dispute-escalation.worker`
(no new escrow/ledger logic), and it re-reads the bet under the worker's advisory
lock and no-ops unless still MATCHED (race-safe against a play/result landing at
the deadline). The **10-minute no-show window is a tunable constant**
(`NO_SHOW_TTL_MS` in `match-lifecycle.ts`), reused from `cleanup-bets`.

## Boundary
Zero `src/lib/ledger/*` changes; reuses `refundEscrow` only.

## Tests
Both players surface the same joinable match with correct roles; the no-show void
refunds both with no locked funds and is idempotent/race-safe. Full suite: 131 passing.

body:
# Description

Two small, independent documentation/CI fixes on one branch.

**#770 — `interpolate_to_raster` advertised a non-existent `pykrige` dependency.** Both the docstring and the
`ValueError` for an unsupported method told users that kriging needs the optional `pykrige` package. `pykrige` is
not a pyramids dependency — it is absent from `pyproject.toml` and never imported anywhere (`grep -rn pykrige src/`
returned only those two lines). Kriging is deliberately out of scope for pyramids (`gdal.Grid`, which this method
delegates to, cannot krige); variograms and kriging live in the sibling **geostatista** package. The message and
docstring now point kriging users there instead of at a dead install path.

**#761 — docs deploys bloat the repo to ~6.2 GB.** ~96% of the object history is the `gh-pages` branch: `mike`
re-deploys a full copy of the built docs per version on every push, and the docs build **executes** the example
notebooks in CI. Two of them dominate:
- `basemap-example` — every cell fetches live OSM / CartoDB / Esri (satellite) map tiles and embeds them as large
  PNGs; it is network-dependent and non-deterministic.

author: benoitc
body:
Periodic compaction, retention and TTL sweeps ran inside the per-database writer's message loop. A large database's compaction (on by default at 1 GB) or a big retention/TTL fold could run for seconds, and every concurrent write blocked behind it and timed out at the default 5s while the write still committed, desyncing effects from errors.

Those sweeps now run in a monitored worker, one per kind, with the periodic timer re-armed on completion; the manual sweep triggers share the worker and defer their reply instead of blocking others. `fold_docs` moves to a caller-side snapshot read (like `get_doc`) and honors `id_prefix`, so a prefix fold no longer degrades into a full scan under the writer (the space janitor's `session:` fold was doing exactly that). Resuming a chunked query now hands the shared snapshot to the successor cursor so the retired cursor can't release it out from under later chunks.

body:
Closes #839.

## What

Implement the second stage of the `issue-work` isolated-workspace lifecycle:
`READY -> AGENTS_RUNNING -> COMMITTED`. Once #838's identity-verified clone is
`READY`, spawn subagents against it under a strict execution contract and
serialize writes to a shared checkout with a single-writer lease. GitHub-facing
mutations (push, PR, merge, cleanup) remain the coordinator's exclusive job.

## Why

Part of #830 (isolated workspace and subagent lifecycle), epic #828. Depends on
#838, which delivered the `READY` clone and the atomic manifest primitive but
explicitly deferred subagent spawn to this stage. This stage turns a `READY`
workspace into supervised subagent execution with safe concurrent-write control;
resume reconciliation and safe cleanup (`PUSHED -> ... -> CLEANED`) build on the
`COMMITTED` state in the final sub-issue #840.

## Where

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `global/skills/_internal/issue-work/scripts/agents.sh` | NEW - Bash reference implementation (sourceable library + CLI). |
| `global/skills/_internal/issue-work/scripts/agents.ps1` | NEW - PowerShell parity port. |
| `global/skills/_internal/issue-work/reference/workspace-lifecycle.md` | Extended - agent prompt contract, coordinator/agent capability split, lease protocol, worktree rule. |
| `tests/issue-work/test-agents.sh` | NEW - 43-assertion bash suite (real local git repo; git-only). |
| `tests/issue-work/README.md` | Extended - #839 test section + AC coverage table. |
| `.github/workflows/validate-skills.yml` | Added one run step after the #838 workspace-test step. |

## How

- `agents.sh` mirrors the #829/#838 convention: `set -uo pipefail`, section
  banners, public `agents_*` / internal `_agents_*` functions, a `GIT_BIN`
  injection seam, and a sourcing guard so tests can source it. It sources
  `workspace.sh` to reuse the #838 atomic manifest primitive for the
  `AGENTS_RUNNING`/`COMMITTED` transitions rather than reimplementing it.
- The agent-prompt contract (`agents_build_prompt`) always carries a normalized
  absolute repo path, the active issue, target branch, baseline commit, an
  explicit write scope, and an ownership/prohibition clause (no push, no GitHub
  CLI, no PR, no cleanup).
- The single-writer lease is `mkdir`-atomic (portable, no `flock`/`jq`),
  owner-checked on release, and fail-safe: a held or ambiguous lease refuses a
  second writer rather than allowing a corrupting concurrent write.
- Per-agent worktrees are provided for the concurrent-writes case only; the
  default is a single-writer lease on the shared checkout. Worktree removal is
  explicit so no orphan blocks the later cleanup stage (#840).
- `agents.sh` contains no GitHub CLI call and never pushes - agents cannot
  perform GitHub mutations by construction.

## Test plan

- `bash tests/issue-work/test-agents.sh` -> 43 passed, 0 failed (wired into CI
  right after the triage and workspace suites). Covers path normalization,
  prompt scope/ownership presence, lease mutual exclusion + fail-safe release,
  worktree add/remove with no orphan, and the manifest state transitions.
- The suite canonicalizes its run root with `pwd -P` so worktree-path
  assertions match git's realpath output on macOS (where `$TMPDIR` lives under
  `/var`, a symlink to `/private/var`); verified green under both a normal and a
  symlinked `TMPDIR`.
- No token-shaped literal is committed: any placeholder identity is assembled at
  runtime, consistent with the #838 test suite.
- `test-workspace.sh` regression: 42 passed, 0 failed.

## Pre-PR gate

- `develop` was unchanged since the working clone (origin/develop == the
  baseline commit), so no rebase/conflict resolution was needed.
- Documentation-to-issue gap audit against the #829/#838 precedent: full
  `SKILL.md` workflow integration, the `CHANGELOG.md` entry, and the
  `docs/.index/` regeneration are intentionally deferred to the
  lifecycle-completing sub-issue **#840**. Rationale: (1) `SKILL.md` and
  `CHANGELOG.md` are doc-indexed / user-facing, so a mid-lifecycle edit would
  document a workflow whose cleanup/resume half is not yet implemented; (2) this
  matches #838, which created `workspace-lifecycle.md` un-indexed and left
  `SKILL.md`/`CHANGELOG.md` for the whole feature; (3) the issue-work
  scripts/reference are not mirrored to `plugin/`, so no `check_references.sh`
  mirror update is required. A single coherent `SKILL.md`/`CHANGELOG` entry
  lands once the lifecycle is whole.

## Notes

- `agents.ps1` is a faithful 1:1 parity port but was **not** runtime-verified
  (no `pwsh` in the authoring environment); it is not executed by any CI step.
  Cross-platform PowerShell regression coverage is integrated in **#832**,
  consistent with the #829/#838 notes in `tests/issue-work/README.md`.

author: leaf-salix
body:
## Summary

This PR reworks the Qwen3-14B prefill driver from a layer-major full-prompt
hidden-state layout into a window-major pipeline.

The previous implementation materialized full packed hidden buffers whose size
scaled with total prefill tokens:

```text
hidden_states      [total_prefill_tokens, HIDDEN]
layer_next_hidden  [total_prefill_tokens, HIDDEN]
```

For long packed prefill, for example batch 16 with roughly 3.5k prompt tokens,
these full hidden tensors grow to hundreds of MiB each. The live input/output
hidden pair becomes a GiB-scale pressure point before layer-local scratch is
counted, which can exhaust PTO2 ring heap and fail with `507018`.

The new implementation keeps KV cache as persistent semantic state, but streams
hidden activations by token window:

```text
for token_window in sequence order:
    window_hidden = embed(token_window)
    for layer in layers:
        window_hidden = layer(window_hidden, per-layer KV cache)
    save final hidden/logits when needed
```

This changes the main hidden activation footprint from
`O(total_prefill_tokens * hidden)` to `O(window_tokens * hidden)`.

## Implementation Notes

- Process prefill tokens in sequence order by bounded windows instead of keeping
  full-prompt hidden states alive across every layer.
- Preserve correctness by keeping per-layer KV cache persistent; only temporary
  layer hidden activations are window-local.
- Keep the existing Qwen tiling shape where possible:
  - attention still uses 64-token subtiles;
  - MLP still uses 128-token tiles.
- Use explicit active-token tiling for partial batches, so a physical
  `[BATCH * 128, HIDDEN]` capacity buffer does not make b1/b4 cases execute fake
  b16 MLP rows.
- Align the Qwen prefill runner DFX flags with the current upstream run-config
  convention.
- Keep the fix scoped to `models/qwen3/14b/prefill_fwd.py`.

Diff against upstream main:

```text

1 file changed, 216 insertions(+), 93 deletions(-)
```


The functional prefill fix was validated at:


`ad298b2` only updates runner/DFX flag handling (`+19/-2`) and does not change
the prefill DSL scheduling logic that the evidence below validates.


| b1 seq128 | PASS | 6.12 | 24.06 | 6.700 | 6.373 |
| b1 seq256 | PASS | 6.11 | 25.77 | 11.677 | 11.327 |

### Performance

Configuration:

```text
no-swimlane

--use-max-seq
repeat=3
```

Baseline results are reused from the existing evidence report. Fixed results
were retested at `961f88c`.

| case | baseline result | baseline device_wall(ms) | baseline sched(ms) | fixed 961f88c result | fixed 961f88c device_wall(ms) | fixed 961f88c sched(ms) | fixed / baseline |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| b1 seq128 | PASS 3/3 | 6.702 | 6.388 | PASS 3/3 | 6.675 | 6.327 | 0.996x |

The `b4 seq256` case is the main active-row regression check. Before
`961f88c`, the fixed branch measured `66.499ms / 2.318x` on this case because
partial batches still executed fake `BATCH * 128` MLP rows. After explicit
active-token tiling, it is back to `31.686ms / 1.105x`.

Detailed run logs are archived in the local evidence report.

### Long Sequence Heap

Configuration:

```text
no-golden

```

|---|---|---:|---:|---|

Detailed run logs are archived in the local evidence report.

- KV cache is intentionally not reduced by this PR. It is persistent model state
  required by later prefill windows and decode. The heap reduction comes from
  bounding temporary hidden activations.
- The stricter `--use-max-seq` b16 seq3500 heap256MiB stress case still hits
  ring3 `507018`. The long-sequence heap result above matches the PR evidence
  configuration used for the upstream baseline/fixed comparison.

author: pawellisowski
body:
Adds a 4th display mode alongside Solid / Wire / X-ray that shades each element from its semantic `material` instead of one flat grey — steel reads as steel, concrete as concrete.

## Why it is not just a table of numbers

Realistic metal is nothing but reflections. Against the existing light rig (`HemisphereLight` + two directionals, no `envMap`), setting `metalness: 1` renders steel **black**. So the mode generates an image-based light in the browser — `RoomEnvironment` → `PMREMGenerator` — and switches on ACES filmic tone mapping. Both are generated from fixed code with no asset fetch, no clock and no randomness, so the byte-determinism guarantee in the module header still holds.

That invariant had **no test**. There is one now.

## Material resolution

`material` is read from the canonical **element-level** field — the same one `ifc::resolve_material` uses — so a scene authored for IFC export shades correctly with no producer change. `meta.material` is accepted as a fallback only.

A grade names the **alloy, not the finish**, so it only decides the look where the alloy *is* the look:

| Input | Family |
|---|---|
| `A240` / `304` / `316` | stainless |
| `A588` / COR-TEN | weathering |
| `6061` / `6063` | aluminium |
| `A123` / `HDG` / `G90` | galvanised |
| `A36` `A992` `A572` `A500` (plain carbon) | **painted** |

`painted` is the default and deliberately has **no colour of its own** — it keeps the element's group colour. Most fabricated steel really is painted, and it means switching to Realistic does not flatten every member to one grey and destroy the profile legend.

## Graceful degradation

If the environment cannot be generated (lost context, a driver without the float targets PMREM needs), the mode falls back to flat shading rather than applying metalness with nothing to reflect — which would render every metal element black, worse than not switching at all.

## Verification

Driven in a **real browser** against a rendered document, not just asserted on strings:

- All 10 material-resolution paths resolve to the correct family, including the `meta` fallback and a whitespace-only canonical value
- `envOn: true` — environment live, ACES active
- Switching back to Solid restores every material **exactly** (no stranded metalness)
- Console clean
- `cargo test`: 729 passed, 0 failed

That pass caught a regression this change introduced: group colours arrive as CSS strings while family colours are numeric, and `Color.setHex` takes only a number — so restoring a group colour through it yielded `NaN` and rendered **everything black in the default Solid view**. Fixed to `.set`, with a guard test.

Reviewed by Codex across 3 rounds; both findings (P1 canonical-field resolution, P2 whitespace fallback) fixed and re-verified behaviourally.

## Not verified

No visual screenshot — capture times out against the software-rendered WebGL loop in this environment (no GPU). Evidence is state-based. First switch measured ~1.9s on that software rasterizer while PMREM warms; every later switch is free, and it is well under 300ms on real hardware.

## Note for reviewers

`cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy` do not pass on clean `main` under the current stable toolchain (20 fmt hunks, 4 clippy errors, all in files this PR never touches). **This diff adds zero new findings to either.** Unrelated files were deliberately not reformatted; tracked separately.

## Problem

Part of the #740 A/V-desync audit. The serve-time `tfdt` anchor rewrites each segment so `seg-N` decodes at `N·segDuration`. That is correct for grid-aligned transcode output but wrong for **remux**, whose segments are keyframe-cut and already carry a `-copyts` timeline — so the slow path deliberately skips it (`skipTimelineRewrite: quality === 'remux'`, #349).

The **on-disk fast path** (`streaming.controller.ts`, the `existing.quality === quality` branch) did **not** pass that flag. Since a segment's first serve goes through the slow path (skipped) but every subsequent re-serve from cache went through the fast path (anchored), the same remux segment was handed out with two different timelines depending on cache state → keyframe-vs-grid shift → seconds of A/V desync against the on-grid audio renditions, on both web (Shaka) and desktop (libmpv).

The slow-path comment even claimed it was "the only remux-reachable tfdt path" — false; the fast path is reachable for remux (its `segName` logic already branches on `quality !== 'remux'`).

## Fix

Pass `skipTimelineRewrite: quality === 'remux'` on the fast-path serve too, and correct the comment. Remux serving is now deterministic and consistent with the slow path.

**Transcode is unaffected** — the flag is `false` for every non-remux rung, so the common path is byte-identical.

## Scope note

This fixes the fast/slow **inconsistency** for cold/forward remux playback. The deeper remux-**after-seek** issue (a remux respawn writes `tfdt=0`; both paths then serve `tfdt=0` against an absolute playlist) is a separate, higher-risk item tracked for the runtime-validation branch, not addressed here.

## Testing

- `streaming.controller` suite: 11 passed. `tsc`: clean.
- Not yet validated on a live remux (DirectStream) playback — behavioural change is confined to remux and aligns it to the already-shipped slow-path contract.

Refs: #740

body:
Closes #28.

## What

Adds a **data-driven set-piece layer** alongside interactive dialogue — the scripted, plot-driven scenes the arc calls for (an escort, a scripted arrival), with no combat/scripting engine: everything lives in a JSON timeline, mirroring Disco Elysium's "it's all in the dialogue/timeline" approach.

## Format — `data/cutscenes/*.json`

```json
{ "id": "escort_departure", "scene": "prison_yard", "timeline": [ ...steps ] }
```

Step types (documented in `scripts/systems/cutscene_runner.gd` and `CLAUDE.md`, enumerated in the validator):

| step | fields | effect |
|------|--------|--------|
| `wait` | `seconds` | hold |
| `line` | `speaker`, `text`, `portrait?`, `seconds` | narration line (no options) |
| `walk` | `actor` (`"player"` or an NPC id), `to` `[px,py]`, `face?`, `speed?` | walk an actor across the backdrop |
| `flag` | `flag` | set a flag |
| `effects` | `effects` | reuses the dialogue `effects` schema |

## How it fits the architecture

- **`CutsceneRunner`** (`RefCounted`, UI-free, unit-tested) sequences the timeline and applies store steps through `dispatch` — the same split as `DialogueRunner` (pure logic + store effects; rendering is someone else's job).
- **`painted_scene.play_cutscene()`** is the only glue: it performs the visual steps (wait/walk/line) and suspends player input + NPC idle-animation while a cutscene runs, then restores control.
- **`Db`** loads `data/cutscenes/`; **the validator** enforces real scene refs, known step types, resolvable walk actors, and valid effects — so a broken cutscene fails CI, not playtest.

## Acceptance

- ✅ Format documented alongside the manifest schema (runner header + `CLAUDE.md`).
- ✅ Demo cutscene — Jailer Ordo escorting the player out of the prison yard — plays **headlessly in the smoke test** (asserts an actor walked and the flag/journal steps applied) and **renders in screenshots** as `08_cutscene`.

## Tests

- `test/unit/test_cutscene_runner.gd` — sequencing, effect application, and that visual steps never touch the store.
- `test/unit/test_content_validation.gd` — cutscene scene/step/actor/effect validation.
- `test/integration/test_playthrough.gd` — runs the shipped cutscene end to end.
- `tools/smoke_test.gd` + `tools/screenshots.gd` — runtime coverage.

Verified locally with `gdformat`/`gdlint`; full runtime verification (smoke test, gdUnit4, screenshots) runs in CI.

author: in-jun
body:
Tightens up the write and conflict-reporting paths in `SyncExecutor` and the two `Storage` backends.

- **#104** — Push/materialize opened a local `Source` and handed it to `writeAtomic` as a separate step. A cancellation landing on `writeAtomic`'s dispatch boundary (routine here — the worker can stop mid-pass) skipped the `finally` that closes it, leaking the descriptor. Each `local.read(...)` feeding a write is now scoped with `use { … }`, so the source is closed even when the write never starts.
- **#97** — `writtenMeta` re-probed the destination and, on a size match, paired *whatever was on disk* with the hash we just wrote. A concurrent same-size overwrite in that window produced an ancestor pairing the interloper's stat with our hash, which the scan hint then trusted forever — silent data loss. `writeAtomic` now returns the stat observed on the file it actually wrote (the temp before its rename locally, the still-open handle on SMB), and `writtenMeta` records that instead of ever re-looking-up the path.
- **#95** — The conflict notification was kind-blind: it told the user "changed on both sides; both versions were kept — open the app to resolve" for path/dir collisions (nothing copied, unresolvable in-app) and for auto-resolved modify-deletes, and the collision path showed up nowhere. Notifications and the last-sync summary are now kind-aware — collisions name the offending path(s) and say to rename or remove one side, and passes with only auto-resolved modify-deletes raise no "resolve" alert.
- **#74** — Adds a crash-point sweep for modify-vs-delete (and its delete-vs-modify mirror) asserting the surviving edit is never lost at any interruption, plus a regression test for the concurrent-overwrite case above. The in-memory fake now reuses the scan hint like the real backends, so the hash-reuse path the bug flows through is actually exercised.

Fixes #104

## Summary

## Issue

UAT pairing on the mock storefront found several broken or confusing surfaces: My Account clicks missed the control, cart badge spacing was wrong, Hero/category/search/PDP layouts looked unfinished, product alias URLs 404’d, sign-in redirect raced, search results were unclear, empty states flashed, footer links were placeholders, and mock copy/CAD labels were mismatched.

## Cause & user impact

Shoppers could not reliably open account sign-in, land on intended redirects after login, open shareable product URLs, or find products from category/search. Layout and copy issues made the demo feel broken even when data was present.

- Header controls lost `flex-col` / absolute badge positioning, so hit targets and badge placement drifted.

書式メニューを **エンコード群** と **行操作** で拡充。すべて純関数で #37 の seam（`selectedText` / `replaceSelection` ＋ `TextTransform`）にそのまま乗る。復号系は不正入力に備え `apply` を Optional 化済み（`nil`＝変換不能＝ビープ・本文不変）。

## エンコード／デコード
- **URL** — RFC 3986 unreserved 以外を % エンコード / `removingPercentEncoding`。
- **Base64** — 折り返し改行入りも復号（`ignoreUnknownCharacters`）、復号後が UTF-8 でなければ変換不能。
- **HTML エンティティ** — encode は `& < > " '` を実体参照へ。decode は数値参照(10進/16進)＋主要な名前付きを**1パス**で復号（`&lt;` を二重復号しない・未知の実体はそのまま残す）。

選択テキストをそのまま行分割して処理（フィルタ ⌥⌘R と同じ考え方・末尾改行を保つ）。

Repositions `/footprint/` from a self-serious personal audit into a plain-English **carbon footprint calculator and visual case study**, and works through a full copy + structure review rather than patching individual lines.

## Naming & metadata
- Browser tab is now **"Carbon Footprint Calculator"**; the product/experience is **"Your Carbon Footprint"**. "Life Footprint" is gone from titles, og/twitter, nav and internal headings.
- Hero rewritten to **"My year of carbon emissions"**; corny/confessional lines removed (e.g. "Counted, not confessed").

## The reveal (now the bulk of the page)
- **Reference points** replace "Guess my number": Australian average, world average, 1.5°C lifestyle benchmark, shown before the total so it lands with context.
- The **FY2026 total reveals immediately** on arrival (no extra scroll). Category chips get a dark translucent tint so they read over the particle field, and a hint makes the interaction explicit ("the glowing dots are its share of the total").
- Short, cute **tCO₂-e explainer** near first use.
- **Scope 1/2/3** rewritten around where emissions come from, with the car example ("If I had a car, the petrol I burned would sit here").
- Hotspots/wedge copy → plain "work on the biggest categories".
- **Benchmarks** reframed: 2.5 t is a 1.5°C-aligned lifestyle benchmark (not a "2030 target"), with a concise note on what 1.5°C means and how national averages differ from a personal footprint.
- **Result/character** section leads with the named result in plain words; "taxonomy" jargon dropped; the three readings relabelled Size / Focus / Timing.
- "What would move it" → **"How could I cut my carbon"**; personal cost-per-tonne figures removed.
- **Sharing**: all shareable cards consolidated into one horizontal gallery at the end so sharing no longer interrupts the reveal. Copy/share asks whether to show a name → "[Name]'s / My FY2026 carbon emissions". Story, square-post and LinkedIn formats all wired.

## Data & structure
- **Travel corrected**: January now holds the North-Asia circuit (Sydney→Tokyo→Shanghai→Tokyo→Seoul→Sydney) plus the Manila trip; February no longer contains Manila; the Singapore leg returns to Sydney, not Melbourne. Annual and month/category/scope values recalculated — **13.3 tCO₂-e total, January the clear worst month**.
- **Public activity log removed** (personal data) and replaced with a compact export / restore / delete controls strip.
- Removed the 45-second/assessor lane and the standalone marginal-abatement-cost curve.
- Dashboard trimmed to supporting detail (totals, month-by-month, category); repeated scopes/result/benchmark blocks dropped.
- Plan simplified to **"biggest practical reductions"** cards (what changes, approx annual saving, difficulty, why) with the pathway chart alongside.

## How it works (basis of preparation)
- Rewritten as a plain **"How the calculator works"** page: what it includes/excludes, sources, how results are calculated, how to read them; exclusions split into outside-boundary / no-reliable-data / optional-extras.
- Removed the made-up factor-set ID, the factor-refresh workflow, the uncertainty-tier table, and personal jokes/details.
- Source naming corrected to **UK Government (DESNZ / DEFRA)**; diet source strengthened with an Australian cross-check and clearly labelled an estimate; petrol factor verified correct.

## Verification
- `npm run build` passes.
- Browser smoke test (Playwright) confirmed: correct tab title and hero, immediate total reveal, tCO₂-e explainer, category hint, 3 reference cards, 5-card share gallery, dashboard/plan render, method page shows no `CW-PF` factor-set ID, no console/page errors.

Note: optional advanced categories (clothing, electronics, hotel nights) are described as optional extras in the method rather than added as new inputs, to keep the default calculator simple and avoid shipping unverified factors.

## Summary

Adds a parametrized test suite for `lib/wallet/config.ts` covering every documented failure mode plus the default fallback and env-var cleanup behaviour — all with explicit `ConfigError` assertions. Closes #134.

## Coverage

| Failure mode | Test |
|---|---|
| Invalid chain name (`mainnet,ethereum`) | rejects with `ConfigError` naming the bad value and listing supported values |
| Empty chain list | whitespace-only CSV falls back to documented defaults (empty-list guard is unreachable from the public surface — documented in the test) |
| Unsupported connector (`walletconnect`, mixed `injected,coinbase`) | rejects with `ConfigError` listing supported values and linking docs |
| Malformed RPC URL (non-URL, non-http(s) protocol) | rejects with `ConfigError` naming the env var and the bad value |
| Default fallback | resolves to `mainnet + base + sepolia`, single `injected` connector, transport per chain |
| Env var cleanup | mutations from one case do not leak into the next |

13 tests across 6 `describe` blocks. All pass.

## Implementation notes

- `test/setup-alias.ts` registers a `Module._resolveFilename` hook that maps `@/lib/...` to the `test-dist` build output. Required because `lib/wallet/config.ts` imports via the `@/` alias which Node cannot resolve at runtime.
- `test/tsconfig.json` gains `lib/wallet/config.ts` in includes, `skipLibCheck: true`, `lib: ["dom", "dom.iterable", "es2022"]`, and `node_modules` exclude so viem's transitive `ox` package type errors don't block the build.

- Tests run in **live** mode (set at module import time before `lib/config.ts` is loaded) so `buildWalletConfig` propagates `ConfigError`s instead of falling back to the mock-mode defaults.

## Summary

- apply quadratic easing and distance-based timing to gems falling after matches clear
- animate refill gems from above the board and clip them at the grid boundary
- share the board-gap value between layout and transform calculations
- respect reduced-motion preferences without retaining invisible swap/drop waits
- cover cascade phases, per-gem distances, refill boundaries, and real-browser clipping

## Why

Falling gems previously shared the same spring transition as swaps, while refill gems scaled into their final cells. Cascades therefore did not read as gravity-driven movement. Moving refill origins above the board also exposed them before they entered play because the grid did not clip animated overflow.

## Impact

Existing and newly generated gems now accelerate as they fall, with longer drops taking proportionally longer. Refill gems remain hidden until they enter the board. Users who request reduced motion skip transform-based animations and their associated waits, while match-clear feedback remains intact.

nothing beyond CI

body:
## Summary
- User, live, after #869/#871 shipped: "why are all the gantt bars the same spot... aren't they supposed to be staggered?"
- Root cause (confirmed with real data): the bar span used to be the true min/max of every element in a storey|phase group. A small fraction (~0.5-1%) of elements per floor carry a real, PRESENT storey tag that disagrees sharply with their own extracted Z (e.g. an `IfcPipeFitting` tagged "Level 5" but physically near Z~164m, below even Level 1's median 168.9 — likely a riser/connector whose IFC "Level" reflects which floor's system it serves, not where it physically sits). `schedule_gate.js` correctly gates these by real geometry, so they schedule almost immediately — but true min/max let that handful of outliers drag the whole floor's bar down to "starts at day 0", even though the bulk of the work (Hospital Level 5: 99%+ of 7,627 elements, median start day 258) is genuinely gradual and staggered by floor.
- Fix: trim the bar's drawn span to the 2nd-98th percentile of real per-element start/end times — still real extracted data, just excluding the extreme 2% each side. Tiny groups (n<=20) keep true min/max.
- Full diagnosis: `prompts/HOSPITAL_4D_SUPERSTRUCTURE_DURATION_ANOMALY.md` Item 6 (bim-compiler repo).
